title: Unified embed-search pagination & error contract for compatibility layer
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Standardize behavior of embeddings and rerank compatibility endpoints so legacy clients and our new SDKs see identical pagination cursors and mapped error codes. Deliver a compatibility shim that normalizes responses, documents the contract, and provides a short migration path for customers depending on older cursor semantics.
background: Several customers and internal integrations expect legacy pagination semantics (opaque 'cursor' strings, deterministic page size behavior) and older error codes for embeddings and rerank endpoints. Inconsistent responses between the new API surface and the legacy compatibility layer have caused client-side pagination bugs and unclear retry behavior. This ticket scopes a compatibility contract and the rollout plan for a shim that preserves parity while we deprecate legacy clients on a predictable timeline.
scope: Define canonical pagination semantics for embeddings and rerank: cursor shape, empty-page handling, and stable ordering requirements
Map internal error classes to customer-facing HTTP status and error codes used by legacy clients (rate_limit, invalid_cursor, backend_unavailable, model_mismatch)
Implement a compatibility shim in the API gateway layer that rewrites responses for the legacy endpoints
Add API docs + SDK examples showing both current and compatibility-layer behaviors
E2E tests and synthetic load tests that exercise pagination edge cases and error mappings
proposed_changes: Treat pagination cursor as stable opaque string that encodes (model_version, result_offset, timestamp) and return 'cursor': null when no more pages
When page_size is omitted, default to 10 for embeddings and 5 for rerank to match older clients
Normalize error responses: return JSON {"error": {"code": "RATE_LIMIT", "message": "..."}} with HTTP 429 for throttling, 400 for invalid cursor, 503 for backend issues
Introduce 'compat_version' query parameter (compat_version=legacy-v1) to opt into shim behavior during rollout
Expose a migration guide and 'inspect_cursor' debug endpoint for troubleshooting during opt-in
api_examples: Legacy success response example: {"results": [...], "cursor": "def456"} or {"results": [], "cursor": null} when finished
New API equivalence: POST /v2/embeddings/query with body {"q": "foo", "page_size": 10, "cursor": "abc123"} returns same semantics when compat_version=legacy-v1 is set
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim returns identical cursor strings for the same dataset and parameters as legacy endpoints under compat_version=legacy-v1
Pagination edge cases: empty results, page_size > available, negative/zero page_size produce documented errors consistent with legacy behavior
Error mapping layer passes a fuzz test that maps 1000 synthetic internal errors to the documented external codes
Integration tests added to CI that run against gateway shim and compare response parity with a recorded legacy fixture
Documentation published in API docs and link to migration guide from customer support playbooks
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design): finalize contract and get signoff from Legal/Support/Security - 1 week
Phase 1 (alpha): deploy shim behind feature flag and enable for internal customers - 2 weeks
Phase 2 (beta): open opt-in compat_version for a subset of external customers, monitor metrics and error rates - 2 weeks
Phase 3 (ga): enable compat_version globally for legacy endpoints and publish deprecation timeline for legacy clients - 1 week
Phase 4 (cleanup): after 90 days, remove shim and require clients to use new API or explicit migration path
migration_notes: Encourage customers to migrate to v2 APIs: provide code samples for JS/Python that decode legacy cursors
Provide 'inspect_cursor' debug endpoint to help customers decode and validate cursors during migration
Support engineering will have an internal runbook mapping common migration failures to remediation steps
qa_notes: Create fixtures for ordered embeddings sets and deterministic rerank outputs to verify cursor stability
Load-test the shim at expected peak concurrency for large pagination sweeps (1000 concurrent clients requesting many pages)
Pen test the inspect_cursor endpoint to ensure it does not leak PII or excessive metadata
notes: Customer-reported bug: INC-7814 - pagination cursor mismatch in search dashboard
